title: Publication-time observability: explicit public dates, cross-database date disagreement, and current-snapshot-only dates

field_inventory.source_of_creation_date: the API returns created_date per work
message.created is the DOI registration timestamp with a full UTC date-time
firstIndexDate / dateOfCreation are indexing-history fields, distinct from the publication date
NONE - efetch output carries no record-creation or index timestamp, which is why first_observed_at is left None on PubMed records
NONE - the Graph API exposes no creation timestamp
NONE - lastUpdateTimeStamp is a mutable marker, not a creation date

openalex.note: positive = the record became visible AFTER the nominal publication date, i.e. a measurable observability lag; negative = the 'publication date' is later than the record's creation (issue-date vs e-pub effects)

crossref.note: positive = the record became visible AFTER the nominal publication date, i.e. a measurable observability lag; negative = the 'publication date' is later than the record's creation (issue-date vs e-pub effects)

europepmc.note: positive = the record became visible AFTER the nominal publication date, i.e. a measurable observability lag; negative = the 'publication date' is later than the record's creation (issue-date vs e-pub effects)

clinicaltrials_gov.note: This is NOT an indexing lag. It is the registry's own queue: the gap between a sponsor submitting the record and ClinicalTrials.gov first posting it. It is a genuine four-clock quantity because the event (the trial starting) is a third, earlier date again.

field_inventory.source_of_creation_date: submit date and QC date are recorded separately from the post date, so the submission->publication lag is measurable for trials
award_notice_date is preserved; no separate record-creation timestamp in the projected fields
NONE usable - dates arrive as template strings such as '1 {{month_08}} 2014'
NONE - no record was ever served (HTTP 403)
